title: CLCON/18/2017 of Dr. Ravindra Pal Singh Negi Vs Om Prakash

paras.text:
CLCON No.18 of 2017
U.C. Dhyani, J.
Mr. Kishore Kumar, Advocate for the
petitioner.
Mr. Sachin Mohan Singh Mehta, Brief
Holder for the State.
By means of present contempt
petition, the petitioner seeks to punish the
respondent/contemnor for willful
disobedience of the judgment and order
dated 01.9.2016 passed by this Court in
WPSB No.36/2016, Dr. Ravindra Pal Singh
Negi vs. State of Uttarakhand & others.
The order sought to be executed is
being reproduced herein below for
convenience:
ëAccordingly, the writ petition is allowed
and the order dated 31.8.2015 passed by
respondent no.2 is quashed. There will be a
direction to the first respondent to convene a
Review Departmental Promotion Committee and
consider the case of the petitioner for promotion on
the post of Joint Director from the date on which
the juniors were recommended. This exercise
should be completed within a period of two months
from the date of production of a certified copy of
this judgment.í
It is the submission of learned
counsel for the petitioner that the casual
approach on the part of respondent should
not be tolerated and strict action should be
initiated against the alleged contemnor.
One of the objectives of contempt
jurisdiction is the enforcement and
compliance of the order of the Court.
This Court, instead of issuing further
notice to the respondent in order to save
time, reiterates the order dated 01.9.2016
passed by this Court and directs the
respondent to comply with the same within
six weeks of production of certified copy of
this order, failing which alleged contemnor
will be liable to face appropriate action
under the Contempt of Courts Act.
Petitioner is directed to place a copy
of this order, as also the order dated
01.9.2016 to remind the respondent that a

duty is cast upon him to do something,
which has not been done.
Contempt petition stands disposed of.
